svg.title: Bridge
svg.desc: Bridge. Split an abstraction from its implementation so both vary independently: m shapes and n renderers need m + n classes, not m × n. Step 1, A class for every pair: One class per shape and renderer pair, 3 × 3 = 9: a new renderer adds a column, a new shape a row. Step 2, Two hierarchies, a bridge: Shape holds a Renderer and draws only with its primitives; renderers never see a shape. 3 + 3 = 6. Step 3, A call across the bridge: Circle calls renderer.circle(50, 50, 40) across the bridge: svg gives <circle>, canvas arc() calls. Step 4, Grow either side: AsciiRenderer draws every shape and Hexagon works with every renderer: 4 + 4 = 8 classes, not 16.

g.text: One class per shape and renderer pair, 3 × 3 = 9: a new renderer adds a column, a new shape a row.
Shape holds a Renderer and draws only with its primitives; renderers never see a shape. 3 + 3 = 6.
Circle calls renderer.circle(50, 50, 40) across the bridge: svg gives <circle>, canvas arc() calls.
AsciiRenderer draws every shape and Hexagon works with every renderer: 4 + 4 = 8 classes, not 16.
a class for every shape × renderer pair
each class mixes what to draw
no pair needs a class of its own
vs Adapter: a bridge is planned up front; an adapter retrofits a mismatch
vs Strategy: same structure, different intent: two growing hierarchies
Abstract Factory: picks a matching renderer
Seen in: JDBC drivers, Qt's QPainter and QPaintEngine
